past_actions.summary: Quietly expand drop-in hours at the center by 6 hours per week — Tuesday and Thursday evenings — framed as a 'community connection night' rather than crisis support. No stigma attached. Coffee, tables, a counselor on soft rotation. Lower the barrier to entry.
past_actions.emotional_state: Contained. Purposeful. There is a steady low-grade alarm underneath the routine — the kind I've learned not to dismiss and not to amplify. I am not afraid. I am watchful. The work feels more urgent than it did six months ago but I am keeping that urgency internal so it doesn't transfer to the people who come to us for steadiness. I am tired in a familiar way. I am not burned out yet but I can see the shape of it from here if I don't pace myself.

past_actions.summary: Contact Maria Santos directly before the emergency council session — not to lobby, but to offer: real intake data from the drop-in hours, anecdotal testimony I can organize, and my center as a potential node in any council-coordinated response infrastructure. Position the community center as operational support for whatever the council decides, not a supplicant. Ask what she needs from me to make the session productive.
past_actions.emotional_state: The announcement landed hard. Not in a way I showed — I was alone when I read it, and I let myself sit with it for about four minutes before I started making notes. Two months. I've been running on a slow-burn vigilance for weeks and now there is a date. That's clarifying in a way that's almost a relief, which I recognize is a strange thing to feel. The ambiguity was its own kind of weight. Now I know what I'm preparing for. There is urgency underneath my calm and I am not suppressing it — I am converting it. The call to Maria feels important and also slightly terrifying, which tells me it's the right move. I'm aware of my low agency pattern: I tend to prepare extensively and then hesitate at the moment of action. I am not going to hesitate this time. I'm making the call today.

past_actions.summary: Compile and deliver anonymized intake data report to Maria Santos as requested. Report covers Community Connection Night attendees (Tuesdays/Thursdays): aggregate demographics, employment status categories, named stressors cited, services requested, and referral needs. Framed explicitly as evidence for the council vote. Delivered in writing within 48 hours — not at the end of the week, not after one more review pass. Within 48 hours.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grounded. There is something steadying about having a specific person ask me for a specific thing by a specific date. Maria asked me for the data in writing. That is not ambiguous. The temptation to over-prepare — to run the report through three more review passes, to wonder if the task force application is strong enough before I send it — is present and I am naming it so I can set it aside. The people who came in Tuesday are not ambiguous either. Harold, who drove taxis for eleven years and does not know how to make a resume. The woman who would not give her name but took the handout. They are why I move fast. Not for myself. For them.

past_actions.summary: Accept Maria Santos's invitation to speak at the task force meeting. Prepare structured testimony specifically addressing who is being left out of existing programs: returning workers without current credentials, gig workers with inconsistent income history who don't qualify for traditional assistance, people with transportation barriers who can't reach program sites, individuals who won't self-identify as unemployed due to stigma, and those displaced by automation (specifically rideshare and taxi workers) who are too old or too resource-depleted to retrain without bridge support. Ground all testimony in anonymized intake data from Community Connection Nights, not anecdote alone. Frame the excluded populations not as failures of individual will but as gaps in program design — this matters for policy, and it matters for how Maria can present it to colleagues who will be resistant.
